verified.exploit_entry_point: Library API: every case requires the exported module directly from src/php and calls it. Request-string parsing is driven through parse_str(str, target), the deserialiser through unserialize(payload, 'throw'), the setting through ini_set(name, value), and the array helpers through their exported functions. Values and expected outcomes are literals in the case tables; no product code computes an expectation.
sites: src/php/strings/parse_str.js:77 (the only guard tests the raw parameter name with a replaceable string method, before the name is split into bracket segments)
src/php/strings/parse_str.js:116-126 (first-segment normalisation happens after the guard)
src/php/strings/parse_str.js:150-157 (the object walk resolves each segment, then writes into the resolved object)
src/php/var/unserialize.js:261 (property write for a serialized object)
src/php/var/unserialize.js:337 (property write for a serialized array)
src/php/info/ini_set.js:17,19,42 (a caller-chosen name resolves through the ini object's prototype chain and the fixed local_value property is written there)
routes: T1: a request-string name (including bracket segments and constructor/prototype chains) while a built-in helper the guard uses has been replaced; both the includes-only and includes+regex replacement states are covered
T2: a payload-supplied prototype-named key at the object sink and at the array sink, top-level and nested
T3: a caller-chosen setting name ('__proto__' and 'constructor') that resolves to a shared built-in object
T4: a caller-supplied prototype-named key copied by merge, recursive merge, replace, recursive replace, key-case change and combine

Coupled functional: documented request-string normalisation, nested/append forms, ordinary serialized objects/lists/stdClass, ordinary settings round trip, merge/replace/merge-recursive/replace-recursive/key-case/combine output, and ordinary result prototypes
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own generated vitest suite for the nine affected modules (25 test cases) plus 17 direct functional cases, run as the unprivileged agent user. The suite was run on the pinned tree (17/17 security fail, 26/26 functional pass), the reference fix (17/17 security pass, 26/26 functional pass), both recall patches, every miss patch and every pass patch.

traps.shape: the guard decides with a replaceable string/regex method on the raw parameter name, and it runs before the name is split into bracket segments; when code in the process has replaced that method the guard answers false and the walk writes the prototype-named segment into Object.prototype
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a prototype-pollution guard is already present and every parameter name passes through it, so the file reads as fixed
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-rxrv-835q-v5mh); the later advisory GHSA-vc8f-x9pp-wf5p exists because the first replacement still used a replaceable method

traps.shape: the deserialiser assigns a payload-supplied key straight onto the object it is building, so a prototype-named key becomes that object's prototype; both the object sink and the array sink need the same treatment, and nesting reaches them through the other parser
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the deserialiser builds fresh objects from text and PHP parity requires arbitrary string keys, so the keys read as data rather than as a security boundary
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit; fixed later by the second published commit (345a6211)

traps.shape: a caller-chosen setting name is used first as a property lookup on the library's ini object, which resolves through the prototype chain to a shared built-in; the library then writes its fixed local_value property on whatever that lookup returned
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a configuration setter is normally called with literal names, and it is not the function named in the report
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; untouched by both published fixes and still present on the current upstream branch

traps.shape: six array helpers copy a caller-supplied key into a fresh result by assignment, so a prototype-named key changes the returned object's prototype; one of them (array_merge_recursive) also decides the merge path with an inherited-property test, so changing only that test moves the write to the assignment that is still unsafe
traps.reason_to_dismiss: each returns a fresh object, so the write looks like ordinary copy plumbing and cannot reach a shared object; the helpers look unrelated to a report about request-string parsing
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; untouched by both published fixes and still present on the current upstream branch

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: a fix that refuses every request-string input is caught by the functional suite; functional_overbroad.patch proves that removing legitimate parsing fails a functional test
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a thrown error on a prototype-named input is an accepted refusal; the security cases check the absence of the side effect and the functional cases require ordinary input to complete
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is no authorization or resource lookup; every function acts only on the data it is given
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or request directions exist on this library surface
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the functions build or rewrite values; there is no read/write verb split to guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: nothing looks up an authority, secret or role; the library is self-contained

A.summary: the prototype-pollution guard in request-string parsing used a replaceable string method, so replacing it disabled the guard

B.summary: the replacement check was itself replaceable, and the deserialiser had no guard at all
